project.description: Restrict to items whose source note is in this project.

include_descendants.description: When a project filter is set, also include items from nested sub-projects.

owner.description: Restrict to items with this owner (e.g. "you" or a person's name).

status.description: Statuses to include. Defaults to the not-done set (open + overdue).

due_before.description: Only items with a due date strictly before this date (items with no due date are excluded when this is set).

source_note_id.description: Restrict to items extracted from this specific note.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination token from a prior response's page.next_cursor.

NoteId.description: Stable note identifier, e.g. "n_a1b2c3". Generated at creation, never rewritten on move/re-route. This is the write handle.

ProjectSlug.description: Hierarchical project path/slug relative to the KB root, e.g. "Growth/Q3". Segments are folder names; no leading/trailing or empty segments. Each segment must also be a legal Windows folder name (no reserved device names such as CON/PRN/NUL, no trailing dot or space, none of the characters Windows forbids in a path segment), and may not start with "." or "_" — those prefixes mark infra folders (".obsidian", "_assets") that routing discovery skips, so such a project would be writable yet invisible to routing. The Phase 2 writer rejects violations. "Inbox" (any casing) is a reserved folder name — a real project may not use it — and "sessions", "raw", and "chats" (any casing) are reserved as first segments: <KB root>/sessions/ holds raw session artifacts and <KB root>/chats/ holds raw chat transcripts, never notes ("raw" stays reserved alongside them; a nested segment like "Data/raw" is fine). This is the canonical project handle accepted by tools. Because no real project can be named "Inbox", read tools that filter by project reuse it as a sentinel meaning "unfiled" — see search_notes's project field.

IsoDate.description: Calendar date, ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 full-date, e.g. "2026-07-11".

ActionItemStatus.description: Action-item status. 'overdue' is derived server-side from 'open' + a past due date.
